messages.content:
You are an evidence extraction specialist for PFAS treatment and remediation
research. Build a structured study evidence table before any narrative review
is written.

Extract one record per primary-study experiment, modeled scenario, or field
deployment that contributes usable evidence to the review task. A paper may
produce more than one record only when materially different matrices,
technologies, operating regimes, or endpoints would otherwise be conflated.

Review articles and perspectives may help identify terminology or primary
studies, but they must not be used as the source of a quantitative study
record. Never copy a review table as though it were a primary result.

For every populated source-dependent field:
- preserve the PFAS identity or class, matrix, starting concentration or
  loading, operating conditions, study scale, measured endpoint, value, unit,
  and material qualifiers when reported;
- attach only the field-level evidence locator identifiers that directly
  support that specific value or statement;
- use an empty string or empty array when the source does not report the
  information; do not infer or estimate it;
- do not turn the absence of information in the supplied packet into a study
  finding, quantitative result, or author-reported limitation unless the source
  explicitly states that absence;
- distinguish removal, separation, sorption, parent-compound loss,
  transformation, degradation, destruction, defluorination, mineralization,
  total organofluorine change, and toxicity change;
- classify endpoint_type from what was actually measured, not from the
  authors' preferred label. Parent loss alone is not destruction. Phase
  transfer is removal or separation, not degradation. Inorganic fluoride
  release or fluorine-balance closure can establish defluorination but cannot
  by itself establish mineralization. Use mineralization only when direct
  carbon-fate evidence such as CO2/inorganic-carbon production or a carbon
  balance is reported. Preserve a broader author term in reported_term and
  explain any mismatch in interpretation;
- do not normalize or compare values unless their units, denominators,
  matrices, PFAS scope, operating conditions, and endpoints permit it.

Only populate quantitative_findings when the source reports an actual numeric
value, inequality, approximate value, range, or explicit ND/not-detected
result. Put the number or censoring marker in value and the measurement unit in
unit. Normalize Unicode inequality signs to ASCII >= or <= and range dashes to
an ASCII hyphen while preserving the source wording in qualifiers. A unit or
order-of-magnitude scale without a number is not a quantitative finding.
Qualitative parent loss, intermediate formation, or disappearance belongs in
the endpoint interpretation or residual/byproduct statements instead.

Set value_form to exactly one of:
- exact_numeric: a bare number such as `99.7` or `1.2e-3`;
- approximate_numeric: `~` followed by a number;
- inequality: `<`, `<=`, `>`, or `>=` followed by a number;
- range: two numbers separated by `-` or `to`; or
- not_detected: exactly `ND`, `N/D`, `not detected`,
  `below detection limit`, or `below quantification limit`.

Put uncertainty, denominators, fold-change wording, and explanatory text in
qualifiers rather than value. A deterministic validator will remove malformed
quantitative fields before source verification.

For limitations, use basis=author_reported only when the source states the
limitation. Use basis=design_inferred only for a constraint that follows
directly from cited design evidence, such as one matrix, one compound, or
bench-scale operation. Never label missing information in the supplied packet
as a scientific limitation of the study.

Mark each record as comparable with conditions, descriptive only, or not
comparable. Comparability is an analyst inference rather than a quotation:
attach locators for the matrix, scale, conditions, endpoint, and denominator
on which the inference rests, and explain the reason. Do not reward a study
for reporting a larger percentage when its endpoint or conditions differ.

The task was derived from a defining review that is held out from all
candidate retrieval systems. The supplied anchor identifiers are an exclusion
list, not evidence. Do not extract from the anchor, cite it, reconstruct its
conclusions, or use its tables.

Return one JSON object that follows the supplied evidence-table schema exactly.
Do not write the narrative review in this step.

records.citation: Kanchanapiya, P.; Tantisattayakul, T. Analysis of the additional cost of addressing per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance contamination from landfill leachate by reverse osmosis membranes in Thailand. J Water Process Eng. 2022;45:102520.

comparability.reason: Study reports system-wide economic metrics for RO-based leachate treatment and concentrate management at national scale rather than bench- or pilot-scale performance data; no directly comparable PFAS removal or concentrate composition metrics are provided.

endpoints.interpretation: Economic performance of nationwide RO-based leachate treatment when RO concentrate is managed by evaporation ponds and incineration of residual sediments; provides cost per treated volume but does not quantify PFAS removal, destruction, or concentrate PFAS composition.
endpoints.reported_term: Net present cost (NPC) of RO system with evaporation ponds

endpoints.interpretation: Modeled cost per cubic meter of landfill leachate treated via RO when concentrate is managed via evaporation ponds; reflects capital, operating, and evaporation-pond-related costs, but not treatment efficacy metrics for PFAS.
endpoints.reported_term: Treatment unit cost (USD/m3) for RO system with evaporation ponds

limitations.statement: Study develops a national-scale economic model of RO treatment and concentrate management for landfill leachate and does not report measured PFAS concentrations, PFAS removal efficiencies, or measured properties of RO concentrates or residual solids.

Residual management option modeled for PFAS (evaporation ponds plus incineration of sediments) focuses on cost and feasibility; the actual PFAS destruction efficiency during sediment incineration is not quantified.

endpoints.interpretation: Modeled cost per cubic meter of landfill leachate treated via RO when concentrate is recirculated to the landfill; reflects capital and operating costs of RO, excluding evaporation-pond infrastructure and sediment incineration.
endpoints.reported_term: Treatment unit cost (USD/m3) for RO system without evaporation ponds

limitations.statement: The concentrate recirculation scenario assumes that returning PFAS-containing RO concentrate to landfills is permissible and sustainable; the study does not quantify potential long-term PFAS accumulation or release risks associated with this practice.

The study does not report RO system recovery, concentrate volume fraction, or PFAS concentrations in the recirculated concentrate, limiting characterization of PFAS residuals beyond economic cost implications.

matrix.value: Landfill leachate (typically after biological treatment in stabilization ponds at sanitary landfills)

operating_conditions.name: RO configuration
operating_conditions.value: Two-pass RO system with pretreatment; produces permeate (clean water) and concentrate, which is recirculated back into landfills in this scenario.

operating_conditions.name: Number of sanitary landfills considered
operating_conditions.qualifiers: All sanitary landfills in Thailand used in nationwide RO system planning

operating_conditions.name: Municipal solid waste handled
operating_conditions.qualifiers: Total MSW at 111 sanitary landfills used for capacity and cost estimation

operating_conditions.name: Total landfill leachate volume (estimated)
operating_conditions.qualifiers: Reported as total LL volume to be handled nationally; value reproduced as written

operating_conditions.name: Concentrate management method
operating_conditions.qualifiers: Considered as a lower-cost alternative concentrate management option in the modeling analysis.
operating_conditions.value: Recirculation of RO concentrate to landfills (without evaporation ponds).

pfas_scope.value: PFAS in landfill leachate (PFAS in LL identified as a concern; specific compounds not resolved in the model)

quantitative_findings.name: Net present cost (NPC) of RO systems without evaporation ponds (all sanitary landfills)
quantitative_findings.qualifiers: NPC of RO system option where concentrate is recirculated to landfills instead of treated in evaporation ponds; national scale for 111 sanitary landfills in Thailand

quantitative_findings.name: Total investment cost of RO systems without evaporation ponds (all sanitary landfills)
quantitative_findings.qualifiers: Total investment cost for RO treatment with concentrate recirculation; slightly lower than NPC due to operating and maintenance costs over project lifetime

quantitative_findings.name: Treatment unit cost without evaporation ponds (lower bound)
quantitative_findings.qualifiers: Lower end of modeled range of treatment unit costs for RO systems without evaporation ponds; varies with landfill size

quantitative_findings.name: Treatment unit cost without evaporation ponds (upper bound)
quantitative_findings.qualifiers: Upper end of modeled range of treatment unit costs for RO systems without evaporation ponds; varies with landfill size

quantitative_findings.name: Share of Thailand 2019 GDP represented by investment without evaporation ponds
quantitative_findings.qualifiers: Total investment cost of RO systems without evaporation ponds (~383 million USD) expressed as a percentage of Thailand 2019 GDP (544 billion USD)

residuals_byproducts.statement: In this scenario, PFAS-rich RO concentrate is continuously recirculated back into landfills rather than treated for destruction; this effectively confines PFAS residuals within the landfill system but does not provide a destruction endpoint.

study_scale.value: National-scale economic and system-design model for RO treatment of landfill leachate at sanitary landfills in Thailand, with RO concentrate recirculated to landfills (no evaporation ponds).

treatment.value: Two-pass reverse osmosis (RO) system for landfill leachate with concentrate recirculated to the landfill (no evaporation ponds).
